messages:
opsbot: :rotating_light: Incident INC-20260307-42 created — significant drop in prefix cache hit-rate for kv-cache-prod in us-west-2. Pager runbook triggered, paging on-call.
jen_oncall: ACK — I'm the primary oncall. Observed spike in backend qps and token-costs, customer-facing latency increased for generation endpoints. Starting triage.
sanjay: on it. first glance: hit-rate graph shows a sharp drop at ~14:04 UTC, sustained. Could be eviction/rewarm failure or a bad TTL rollout.
maria: I can pull the per-prefix hit-rate and recent rewarm job logs. Giving me 10m.
eli: tagging product & support: if customers are seeing steady errors we might need to update status page. @paul_incident can you shepherd comms?
paul_incident: yup, ready. Need confirmation of impacted customer list + ETA for mitigation before I post.
jen_oncall: quick mitigation options — (1) enable fallback routing to dedicated pool for high-SLA customers, (2) temporarily increase cache retention for affected prefixes, (3) trigger a targeted rewarm job. Which is lowest risk?
sanjay: (3) rewarm targeted prefixes is lowest risk. But if the rewarm system is failing, (1) might be necessary. I'll validate rewarm job status.
maria: logs pulled. devlogs-bot: shared link -> https://logs.redwood/prod/kv-cache/us-west-2/1759876543
devlogs-bot: snippet:
```
2026-03-07T14:03:58Z INFO prefix="user:account:*/emb" hit=false reason="miss-after-eviction" keycount=0
2026-03-07T14:04:02Z WARN rewarm-job id=rw-993 exit_code=1 stderr="OOM while allocating kv-buffer"
2026-03-07T14:04:04Z ERROR kv-store eviction storm triggered candidates=10234 reclaimed=0
```
maria: raw indicates rewarm job exited with OOM around the same time. hypothesis: rewarm worker OOM -> rewarm failure -> traffic sees cold prefixes -> mass misses -> backend surge -> eviction loop.
eli: what's the customer impact? errors/latency numbers?
jen_oncall: from infra metrics: 5xx for generation routes up from 0.02% to 1.3% for the last 30m; p95 latency increased by ~420ms for the same window. A few enterprise customers reporting degraded response time.
paul_incident: OK, will draft status: "We are investigating increased latency on generation endpoints; mitigation steps underway" — hold until we have mitigation plan.
sanjay: running rewarm job status:
```
$ k get pods -n rewarms | grep rw-993
rw-993  CrashLoopBackOff  4 (OOMKilled)
$ kubectl logs rw-993 -n rewarms
OOMKilled while processing workload chunk size=512
```
sanjay: seems memory pressure on rewarm workers. Stacktrace suggests a regression in recent rewarm-worker image (last deploy ~12:00 UTC).
jen_oncall: roll back rewarm-worker image to previous tag as hotfix? That will restore rewarm capacity, but we also need immediate fallback for impacted prefixes.
maria: I can bump the per-prefix TTL for the top-200 prefixes with highest request rate to 24h (currently 1h) — that'll keep them warm while we fix rewarms. Will take ~3-4m to push.
eli: checklist for mitigation order: 1) roll rewarm worker back (sanjay), 2) bump TTL for top prefixes (maria), 3) monitor hit-rate recovery & backend errors, 4) enable dedicated fallback for enterprise customers if still degraded (jen_oncall/paul).
sanjay: rolling back rewarm worker now — patching deployment to image tag v2.15.8 -> v2.15.7
devlogs-bot: deploy event: rewarms/deployment patched by sanjay at 14:12 UTC -> rollout started.
jen_oncall: maria, execute TTL bump when you have the list.
maria: TTL bump applied for top 200 prefixes. Command used:
```
POST /admin/cache/ttl-bulk HTTP/1.1
Host: cache-api.internal
Content-Type: application/json
{"prefixes": ["user:account:12345/*", "user:account:67890/*", ...], "ttl_secs": 86400}
```
maria: confirm: kv-cache hit-rate starting to climb back up, p95 latency trending down.
sanjay: rewarm deployment rolled back successfully, pods restarting with previous image; rewarm logs show successful allocations now.
devlogs-bot: rewarm logs snippet:
```
2026-03-07T14:14:30Z INFO rewarm-worker id=rw-993 allocated=3 shards status=ok
2026-03-07T14:15:12Z INFO rewarm-job id=rw-993 completed prefixes=198 warmed=192
```
jen_oncall: good. ongoing monitoring for next 20m. paul_incident can proceed with status update (note: mitigation in progress, no reported data loss).
paul_incident: posted status page update: "Partial latency degradation observed; mitigation in progress. No data loss."
eli: recording timeline items for RCA: 14:03 rewarm job OOM -> 14:04 eviction storm -> 14:12 rollback -> 14:15 rewarm success -> recovery.
maria: saving charts and queries to incident docs: https://confluence.redwood/incident/INC-20260307-42/timeline
jen_oncall: outstanding action items:
- sanjay: post deploy diff and rollout logs + confirm root cause in CI for rewarm worker image (assigned)
- maria: upload exact prefix list and TTL change diffs (assigned)
- eli/paul_incident: customer impact roster + comms (assigned)
- opsbot: schedule oncall postmortem in 48h and add RCA owners (opsbot)
opsbot: Postmortem scheduled for 2026-03-09T15:00Z; owners set: sanjay, maria.
sanjay: quick note on hypothesis tracking: primary = regression in rewarm-worker memory usage (likely bad change in chunking / buffer management). Secondary = sudden traffic skew to very large prefixes causing rewarm OOM. I'll bisect the deploy and share PRs.
maria: adding logs + sample request traces to the confluence doc. attaching grep query used:
```
index=kv-prod "miss-after-eviction" | stats count by prefix | sort -count | head 200
```
eli: for RCA we need to quantify customer impact window and token cost delta; I'll pull billing/usage delta for the window 14:00-14:30 UTC.
paul_incident: will coordinate follow-up comms after RCA. Closing live thread — switch to postmortem channel for deep-dive.
jen_oncall: thanks team. Marking incident as mitigated at 14:18 UTC. Will keep monitoring for 1h then declare resolved.
